item.title: Positive recurrence of weakly reversible stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics
item.description: arXiv:2611.32819v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study finite stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. A network is weakly reversible if every reaction lies on a directed cycle of complexes. We prove that, for arbitrary positive rate constants, the Markov chain of every such network is non-explosive and positive recurrent on each communicating class. This settles the long-standing chemical recurrence conjecture. The proof is by construction of a Lyapunov function. For a fixed choice of weights on the species, the function is the exponential of a weighted count of the molecules, adjusted by a bounded quantity which is defined through the paths of reactions leading back to a reference population, and which accounts for the species that are absent or scarce. Before the adjusted count can decrease, several preparatory steps may be needed. We count faster and slower steps separately, giving priority to paths that require fewer slow steps. Weak reversibility controls how competing reactions can change these counts. Finitely many choices of weights are then combined, and a minimization over a scale parameter gives a single function on each communicating class.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Cappelletti, Giulio Cuniberti
